proposals.observation: Of 4 quiz starts in the last 48 hours, 2 people reached the intro screen and went no further. Zero completions across all 6 sessions. The furthest_step_distribution shows equal weight at intro_load and q1_shown, meaning the intro screen itself is a wall. The current text (below) opens with a generic promise that any quiz on any coaching site could carry. It passes no Sultanic test and gives someone no reason to believe the next 90 seconds is different from every other "discover your money type" prompt they've already ignored.
proposals.proposal: Replace the intro screen headline and subhead with copy grounded in the specific sensory reality Joel's ICP lives in: the pay slip arriving, the tab left closed, the number they could check but don't. The goal is to make someone on that screen feel named before they've answered a single question. One file, two text nodes changed. No new components, no logic changes.
proposals.current_text:
Discover your money personality

Answer 7 quick questions and find out what's really driving your financial behaviour.
proposals.new_text:
What's the story you tell yourself about money?

Seven questions. Honest answers. Joel built this from MSc Behavioural Economics research and a decade of client work, because most people earning well still have a tab they haven't opened in three months.

proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three active sequences: 60 percent against a cohort of 10 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 50 percent across 18 sends. Money Worship trails at 37.5 percent across 16 sends. Vigilance readers are the most engaged group right now, yet if the first email in that sequence ends without a clear, specific next step rooted in what vigilance actually feels like day-to-day, that open-rate advantage converts to nothing. High opens with no click data reported means the CTA is either absent or too soft to register.
proposals.proposal: Add a closing paragraph to email-1 in the Money Vigilance sequence that names the lived experience of vigilance (the checking, the rechecking, the spreadsheet that gets updated at 11pm) and offers the consultation as the honest next move. One file, additive change at the bottom of the email body. No automation logic touched.
proposals.new_text:
If any of this sounds like your Tuesday evening, the next step is a free 30-minute call with Joel. Not a sales call. A proper look at what the vigilance is protecting you from, and whether that protection is still doing useful work.

Book at wayofwealth.co.uk/call. Joel holds a limited number of these each week.

Joel

proposals.observation: A blog post was committed today: "Why do I want a budget app that shows what I have LEFT — not what I've spent?" The title is good, it names a real psychological distinction (prospective framing vs. retrospective accounting) that sits squarely in behavioural economics. But a blog post that ends without routing the reader anywhere is a dead end. Given that quiz completions are currently zero and the quiz is the top-of-funnel diagnostic, the post should close with a direct, non-pushy pointer to the quiz that earns the connection rather than demanding it.
proposals.proposal: Add a closing section to today's blog post that connects the prospective-framing insight from the post body to the quiz, without using any of the banned buzzwords and without a generic call to action. One additive file edit at the end of the post content, before any existing footer or tag block.
proposals.new_text:
If you found yourself nodding at the idea of watching forward rather than backwards, that instinct is worth paying attention to. The way you want your money to feel is data. Joel built a short quiz that helps identify the pattern underneath it, the script that decides whether you look or look away. It takes about two minutes.
